description: Error-taxonomy vectors. Each case maps an HTTP outcome (or a client-side validation input) to the taxonomy type every SDK must surface: 'api' (an HTTP error response), 'transport' (no HTTP response was ever obtained), or 'validation' (rejected client-side — a bad input before any request, or a response payload the SDK cannot faithfully represent). 'batch' cases drive the POST /batch per-operation error path under an outer HTTP 200. See conformance/errors/README.md for the loader contract. All 'api' and 'transport' cases are driven with retries disabled (single attempt) so the outcome is deterministic.

body.title: idempotency key reused with a different payload

expect.title: idempotency key reused with a different payload

api.name: server-error-terminal
api.note: 500 is retryable, but with retries disabled the first (only) attempt is terminal and surfaces as an API error carrying the real status 500 — NOT a transport error (a response did arrive).

transport.name: no-response-network-error
transport.note: The transport raises/never yields an HTTP response on every attempt. After the single attempt this must surface as the transport type, and MUST NOT be an API error with status 0/null.

batch.name: per-op-error-with-status
batch.note: HTTP 200: the batch was accepted, but one operation failed with a problem carrying `status`. Surfaces as the SDK's api type with that status/title (+ problem details where the type carries them) — exactly as if the operation had failed standalone. The `applied` sibling result must not mask it.

batch.name: per-op-error-missing-status
batch.note: The per-op problem omits `status` — wire-legal (Problem.status is optional in openapi.yaml) though the current server always sets it. No failing HTTP status exists, so an api error cannot be constructed (an api error carries status >= 400, never 0/fabricated): the SDK rejects the problem it cannot faithfully represent via its validation type.

batch.name: per-op-error-without-problem
batch.note: A per-op `error` with no problem object at all — same rule as per-op-error-missing-status: validation type, never an api error with a 0/absent status.
